WORDING: instructions come from the codebook label for other.fear, 'To what extent do you think most people in [country] are afraid of AI being [occupation]? Please give your best estimate.', with [occupation] replaced by '...' because the occupations are the rows. The paper writes the stem the same way ('...afraid of AI being ...?'). [country] is the codebook's own placeholder, kept as written. Anchors 0 = 'Not at all afraid' and 100 = 'Extremely afraid' come from the paper's Procedure section ('again on a 100-point scale ranging from 0 = Not at all afraid to 100 = Extremely afraid'); the materials PDF's own-fear slider shows the same anchors. resp 1-99 are unlabelled slider points and their option_text is left blank. The English materials PDF does not include the other-fear block. Its own-fear block labels the rows with the full descriptions (e.g. 'A doctor, who is qualified to treat people who are ill.'). The other-fear rows probably looked the same but that is undocumented, so the terser codebook labels are shipped. LANGUAGE: the paper says materials were forward/back-translated wherever the survey ran in a non-English-speaking country, but it names no languages. The deposit holds only English survey text, so English (the version used in the US/UK/Australia/Canada/NZ/Singapore/Nigeria/South Africa/India samples) is the base. The language list is INFERRED from the 20-country list plus the deposit's subtitle files (Rus, Zho-CN, Zho-SG, Fre, Fre_Ca, Kor, Spa-MX, Tur, Por-BR, Hin); German, Italian, Japanese and Arabic are inferred from the country alone.
